liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (3 reviews): Reviewer recommends the China Cat into I Know You Rider pairing; The China Cat into Rider jam is described as truly inspired [12][13][18]
- **Mexicali Blues** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out Mexicali Blues as a strong version; Mexicali Blues is called very fine, possibly one of the best [11][21]
- **Passenger** (2 reviews): Reviewer's favorite stretch is Passenger into Ramble On Rose into The Music Never Stopped; Passenger, Ramble On Rose and The Music Never Stopped are called the show's prize stretch [18][20]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (1 review): The opener ran nearly twenty minutes [22]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Reviewer calls The Music Never Stopped a strong version [11]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): Reviewer recommends Playin' and its move into space; says Jerry wailed [12]
- **Drums** (1 review): Drums ends with a nice surprise [13]
- **Space** (1 review): Brent's synthesizer effects arrived in Space in a far from subtle way [22]

## The recordings

- **gd79-10-28.rolfe.vernon-pujol.19590.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 19 songs; 173 min; rated 3.6/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1979-10-28.145465.fob.nak700.rolfe.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 18 songs; 172 min [4]
- **gd79-10-28.sbd-aud.braverman.7602.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 17 songs; 159 min; rated 4.52/5 by 25 [6]. Said about its sound: Vocals are mostly in tune; recording and performance quality rank among the best in the reviewer's collection; The last six tracks of this matrix come from the audience source; The second-set switch to the audience source disappoints a bit but conveys the party energy [15][17][20]
- **gd1979-10-28.134396.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 181 min; rated 4.67/5 by 3 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls the Coliseum as a sweaty, gymnasium-like hall; general admission gave plenty of room to dance [17]
- The small skating-rink-like Coliseum has since become a warehouse for the Christmas Tree Shops [22]
- After dozens of shows in this collection, reviewer rates this as clearly one of the best [15]
- Reviewer thought 1979 shows were among the weakest, so this one was a surprise [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd79-10-28.rolfe.vernon-pujol.19590.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Rolfe; source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Recorded by Steve Rolfe using a Sony D5 with Nakamichi 700 microphones; Audience master cassette went to DAT via David Minor; Marc Pujol made the WAV transfer; Matt Vernon encoded SHN [1]
- **gd1979-10-28.145465.fob.nak700.rolfe.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Steve Rolfe; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Steve Rolfe's Master (FOB) Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony D5M [4]. Also: A 13-second patch in the Drums to Space transition comes from a Nakamichi 300 source, shared by Doug Morrone and Andrew F [4]
- **gd79-10-28.sbd-aud.braverman.7602.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [6]
- **gd1979-10-28.134396.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Cassette -> Dat [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by blogbujero.blogspot.com: [(009071) Grateful Dead 1979-10-28 Cape Cod Coliseum, South Yarmouth, MA (2 Sources) (FLAC)](https://blogbujero.blogspot.com/2023/11/009071-grateful-dead-1979-10-28-cape.html) [28]
